newsitem.title: FRANCE: EU releases more barley for Saudi, maybe Iran soon.
newsitem.headline: EU releases more barley for Saudi, maybe Iran soon.

text.p: A European Union barley award at this week's tender brings to around one million tonnes the volume of European barley to be shipped to Saudi Arabia under the kingdom's last major purchase, traders and officials said.
The award, higher in volume than many had expected, may also provide scope for barley sales to Iran, suffering the aftermath of last Friday's destructive earthquake, they said on Friday.
The EU granted licences for 398,000 tonnes of free-market barley exports at Thursday's tender at a maximum refund of 26.98 Ecus per tonne.
The award values barley at $132 per tonne fob France.
It includes 100,000 tonnes taken through Spain, where a grain vessel was loading at Valencia this week, traders said.
Saudi Arabia bought 1.2 million tonnes of optional-origin feed barley in January for delivery in February and March.
Although the EU is the main supplier, logistical problems in other areas allowed it a bigger share of the deal than expected and strengthened a positive export year, an EU official said.
"For us the barley campaign was a great campaign this year," the official said, noting that export commitments had risen nearly four-fold compared to the same point last year.
EU figures compiled before the tender show export commitments between July 1 and March 4 stood at 4.549 million tonnes compared with 1.248 million a year before.
Of the 1.2 million tonnes bought in January, the U.S. is expected to supply 150,000 tonnes and Canada, facing a harsh winter and port delays, 50,000 tonnes, traders said.
Traders said attention was beginning to focus on whether Saudi Arabia, the world's largest barley importer, would soon go back to the grain market for later delivery periods.
One trade official said there was no word of a new Saudi tender so far but further purchases soon seemed "logical".

The EU would also be well placed to supply barley needed by Iran to feed 200,000 head of livestock in the quake-stricken northwest, he said, although it was unclear how much, if any, would be part of an international relief operation.
Iran on Wednesday appealed for 100,000 tonnes of barley and said it wanted 70 tonnes each of wheat and barley seed.
The U.N. has said the Tehran government would prefer local purchases where possible.
Brussels-based trade group Coceral is forecasting total 1996/97 (July/June) barley and product exports from the EU of 8.3 million tonnes, up from 4.5 million tonnes last season.
In other coarse grain sales on Thursday, the EU awarded 23,50 tonnes of oats at a maximum 29.34 Ecus per tonne.
Traders said the award -- worth $112 to $115 per tonne -- would cover Finnish oat sales to the U.S.
